result.title: Uncovering the Tells: Efficient Black-Box Audits for LLM Data Contamination
result.summary: Existing methods for assessing training data contamination in Large Language Models achieve high accuracy, but fundamentally rely on gray-box access, rendering them inapplicable to fully black-box environments. This limitation forces auditors to rely on full-sequence sampling or rigid heuristics, both of which incur prohibitive inference costs and struggle to isolate the underlying memorization signal. To overcome this, we propose a generation-based black-box framework that infers context-induced information gain from targeted token discrepancies. We introduce a budget-constrained auditing regime, building on the empirical observation that the membership signal is highly sparse and concentrated in a few highly informative tokens. We formalize this sparsity, showing why uniform sampling needs many more samples than a policy that targets informative positions. Empirically, our approach achieves state-of-the-art black-box separation accuracy while needing about 3x fewer queries than uniform position sampling. Finally, we apply this methodology to closed frontier models, exploring its capacity and limits in surfacing potential training data overlaps on commercial APIs.

AI.brief_summary: 提出纯黑盒的生成式审计框架，通过目标 token 的差异推断上下文诱导的信息增益，并在查询预算约束下利用成员信号稀疏、集中于少数高信息 token 的特点来检测训练数据污染。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「稀疏高信息位置 + 预算约束采样」的思路可能与 LVR 中该探测哪些位置或视觉证据、如何在有限查询内分配计算与停止获取证据有概念联系，但属较远领域，迁移价值仅供核查。
